text:
cheng: Quick recap — ran a SmoothQuant + activation-aware quant (hybrid) on the new 70B long-context build, target ctx=50k, KV prefix caching on. Observed unexpected accuracy drift past ~30k tokens and some tail latency jitter. Posting short notes and logs below.

priya: Can you paste the top-line numbers? which quant stacks did you compare?

cheng: Baseline FP16, SQ-int8 (act-aware smoothing applied at merge points), AWQ-int8, and GPTQ-4bit mix (layerwise). Key config: act_smooth=0.015, reorder=false, kv_cache_eviction=disabled (default), batch=1, seq_len_dist skewed to long tails.

cheng: Quick metric snapshot (eval on long-doc QA + passage-retrieval set):
```
Model             | MMLU acc | QA EM | PPL (lm) | latency p95
FP16 baseline     |  83.4%   |  72.1 |  12.3    |  210ms
SQ-actaware int8  |  81.6%   |  68.9 |  13.1    |  225ms
AWQ-int8 fallback |  82.2%   |  70.3 |  12.8    |  220ms
GPTQ-4bit mixed   |  80.9%   |  66.7 |  14.5    |  195ms
```
Note: the EM drop for SQ-actaware becomes larger when sequence position >30k (we sliced eval by prefix length).
```
(when prefix >=30k) SQ-actaware EM -> 65.1 (vs 68.9 overall)
```

sasha: Interesting — so AWQ-int8 is safer on tail QA but slightly slower than GPTQ mix? I assume GPTQ regressed accuracy more but had lower latency.

cheng: Exactly. GPTQ-4bit mixed keeps latency down but hurts QA EM and PPL more. The unusual part for SQ-actaware: we see KV-cache drift — that is, activation scales diverge over long prefixes, causing numeric mismatch in quantized matmuls when KV re-use happens.

priya: Any logs showing activation scale drift or layerwise per-token scale?

cheng: Pasting sample trace for layer attn.kv_scale_norm (trimmed):
```
token_idx  scale_mean  scale_std
10000      0.021       0.003
20000      0.023       0.004
30000      0.038       0.011   <-- spike
40000      0.040       0.012
```
Spike coincides with docs containing repeated long numerical tables (high-magnitude tokens).

eva: Did you try act smoothing higher or enabling reorder? could smoothquant param tuning recover tail?

cheng: Ran grid: act_smooth in {0.01,0.015,0.03,0.06}. 0.03 improved tail EM (from 65.1 -> 67.8) but introduced slight quality regressions earlier (MMLU -0.6 vs baseline). Reorder=true helped a bit for attention kernels but increased peak memory during compilation.

sasha: What about a runtime mitigation? TTL/evict KV shards beyond 32k or soft reset of prefix cache when scale drift > threshold?

cheng: I prototyped a soft-reset policy: if global scale variance > 0.01 for 5 consecutive tokens, flush KV for layers 10-15 (mid-attn). This recovered EM to 69.8 on the failure slice but caused a visible latency spike (temporary) and micro-hiccup on streaming clients.

priya: For deployment, maybe hybrid policy: SQ-actaware for normal range with AWQ fallback on detected drift, plus canary with kv-ttl=32k and soft-reset on threshold.

perf-bot: Automated canary run results: SQ-actaware (act_smooth=0.03) + kv-ttl=32k + AWQ-fallback triggered in 3.2% of requests; end-to-end error rate unchanged. 24h cost delta +6%.

cheng: TL;DR recommendations:
- Short-term: Canary rollout with AWQ fallback and kv-ttl=32k, act_smooth=0.03
- Medium-term: instrument per-layer token-scale telemetry + adaptive act_smooth scheduler (increase smooth when drift detected)
- Research: explore mixed-precision KV storage (store FP16 for select layers) and better input-conditioned scale estimators.

eva: Agree. Also add integration tests that simulate long repeated numeric tables to catch this in CI.

priya: I'll draft the canary plan + runbook. Cheng can you add the per-layer telemetry PR?

cheng: On it, will open PR with sample visualizations and the soft-reset prototype.

sasha: For release note: call out SQ tail-risk for long numeric-dense docs and recommended config. :warning:

eva: Thanks — good triage.

perf-bot: Scheduled longctx perf sweep: 50k/60k/70k run queued (ETA 6h).
